items.definition: An overarching policy that manages security as an ongoing cycle, using the Plan-Do-Check-Act loop from ISO 27001.
items.examples: An organisation reviewing and improving its security measures every quarter using PDCA.
items.examTip: Plan-Do-Check-Act = continuous improvement. Security is never 'finished' because threats change (link A1.4).
keyFacts: Based on the Plan-Do-Check-Act loop (ISO 27001:2013)
Treats security as a continuous, repeating cycle
Covers internet/email use, passwords, staff responsibilities and training

items.definition: Rules governing acceptable use of internet and email at work.
items.examples: Banning download of executable files; warning that the organisation may scan traffic and retain emails.
items.examTip: Covers offensive/illegal material, sending confidential info, copyright, dangerous sites, and monitoring rights.
keyFacts: No inappropriate, offensive or illegal material
Rules on sending confidential information and privacy
No upload/download of copyrighted material or risky executables
Organisation's right to scan traffic and retain emails

items.definition: The rules and tools that enforce strong passwords and secure account behaviour.
items.examples: Deny lists blocking common passwords; lockout after failed login attempts; logging password attempts.
items.examTip: A password policy should include: length/strength, sharing rules, uniqueness/reuse, lockout, minimum age, expiry (sample paper Q4a).
keyFacts: Length/strength policy and enforcement tools
Deny lists of common/weak passwords
Monitoring/logging of password attempts; lockout policy
Using technology to reduce reliance on passwords

items.definition: What staff must do for security, and how the organisation trains them.
items.examples: Staff completing annual security training and reporting suspicious emails.
items.examTip: Effective training is ongoing, flexible, uses varied resources, tracks progress, and uses incentives not punishment.
keyFacts: Staff: complete training, follow procedures, report suspicious activity
Training should be funded, flexible and ongoing
Use incentives rather than punishment; track progress
Refresh training for new threats

items.definition: Checks that verify whether the organisation is complying with its security policies and external regulations.
items.examples: An audit finding that several accounts still belong to ex-employees.
items.examTip: An audit identifies gaps/weaknesses and checks compliance against internal policies AND external laws.
keyFacts: Defined audit goals and scope
Identifies problems/gaps/weaknesses
Checks against internal policies and external laws
Reports results and required improvements

items.definition: A documented policy defining what data is backed up, how, how often and who is responsible.
items.examples: A policy requiring nightly incremental backups, weekly full backups, and quarterly restore tests.
items.examTip: A good backup policy includes testing (restores) and legal compliance — not just doing the backups.
keyFacts: Selection of data, backup methods and type
Frequency/scheduling and storage strategy
Responsibility/accountability and backup testing
Legal compliance and emergency/recovery procedures

items.definition: A policy ensuring the organisation complies with data protection law (GDPR).
items.examples: Appointing a Data Protection Officer and applying the policy to external contractors too.
items.examTip: Links to GDPR (A3). Key elements: DPO, following principles, protecting rights, staff training, accountability.
keyFacts: Appoint a Data Protection Officer
Follow data protection principles and protect rights/privacy
Staff training and system security procedures
Applies to external contractors/vendors too

items.definition: A plan for how the organisation responds when a security incident occurs.
items.examples: A flowchart for triaging an incident, plus a contact list including legal, PR, HR and insurance.
items.examTip: Response stages: triage/escalation → analysis, containment, mitigation, recovery → review/report/close.
keyFacts: Contacts: response lead, IT, senior management, legal, PR, HR, insurance
Procedures: triage/escalation; containment/mitigation/recovery; review/close
Communications: backup contact numbers, conference facility

items.definition: A policy for recovering systems and operations after a major disruptive event.
items.examples: Triage deciding whether to activate the incident response, business continuity or full disaster recovery plan.
items.examTip: Disaster recovery includes triage (rating event severity), defined roles, contact lists and monitoring.
keyFacts: Defined purpose and scope
Triage: list possible events, their severity and response
May activate incident response, business continuity or DR plan
Clear roles, responsibilities and contact lists

items.definition: A policy governing the use of external providers for cloud, hardware, software and support.
items.examples: A service-level agreement specifying response and fix times for an outsourced support provider.
items.examTip: Covers cloud, hardware, software and support — including SLAs (service time, response time, escalation).
keyFacts: General: authorisation, accountability, contacts, compliance, incident response
Cloud: resources to protect, acceptable use, data protection
Hardware/software: vendors, service agreements, licensing, support
Support SLAs: service time, response time, fix time, escalation
